units.title: The History of the Telephone
units.script:
Narrator: Listen to a talk about the history of the telephone.
Man: The telephone is one of the most important inventions in human history. It allows people to communicate with each other over long distances. Alexander Graham Bell is widely credited with inventing the first practical telephone in 1876. In the past, telephones were large and usually stayed in one place. People could only make calls using wires. Today, telephones have become smaller and more advanced. Smartphones allow people not only to make calls but also to send messages, take pictures, and access the internet. The telephone has changed the way people communicate in their daily lives.

Students can learn how to organize sentences and develop ideas by reading different types of texts. Finally, reading also increases knowledge because books contain information about many subjects, such as science, history, and culture. units.title: Weather and seasons.
units.script:
Narrator: Listen to a talk about weather and seasons. Man: There are four main seasons in many countries, like Europe: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Each season has different weather conditions. Spring is usually warm, and many flowers begin to grow. Summer is generally the hottest season, and people often enjoy outdoor activities. In autumn, the weather becomes cooler, and leaves change color before falling from trees. Winter is usually the coldest season, and some countries experience snow. However, not all countries have four seasons. For example, Indonesia has two main seasons: the dry season and the rainy season. The rainy season usually brings more rainfall, while the dry season has less rain.
Pause: 5

reading.directions: In this section you will read several passages. Each passage is followed by questions about it. Answer each question on the basis of what is stated or implied in the passage.

parts.title: Reading Passages

units.title: Urban trees
units.passage:
Urban trees provide benefits that extend beyond their appearance. Their leaves provide shade, reducing the heat absorbed by streets and buildings. Trees also help manage rainwater: some water is ***intercepted*** by leaves, while roots improve the soil's ability to absorb rainfall.

However, planting trees in cities requires careful planning. A tree that grows well in a park may not be suitable for a narrow sidewalk where roots could damage pavement or underground pipes. Successful urban forestry therefore depends not simply on planting more trees, but on choosing appropriate species and caring for them over time.

units.title: Tan Malaka and His Ideas
units.passage:
Tan Malaka was an Indonesian nationalist who played an important role in the struggle for independence. He was born in West Sumatra in 1897. During his life, he traveled to several countries and studied different political and social ideas. He believed that education was important for improving society. He also wanted Indonesia to become an independent nation.

Tan Malaka wrote many books and articles. One of his famous works is Madilog, which discusses materialism, dialectics, and logic. His ideas ***influenced*** many people who wanted to fight against colonialism. However, his political activities sometimes brought him into conflict with other leaders.

Tan Malaka died in 1949, but his ideas remain important in Indonesian history. Many people study his writings to understand the development of Indonesian nationalism.

units.title: Salman Kancil and Environmental Protection
units.passage:
Salman Kancil was a young boy from East Java who became known for his efforts to protect the environment. He opposed illegal sand mining in his village because the activity damaged the land and threatened the local community. Sand mining can cause ***erosion*** and change the natural condition of rivers and nearby areas.

Salman was concerned about the future of his village. He believed that people should protect natural resources for the next generation. His actions attracted public attention and became an example of the courage of young people who speak about environmental problems.

Environmental protection requires cooperation between citizens, local governments, and businesses. People can help by reporting illegal activities and supporting responsible use of natural resources.

units.title: The Bali Bombing and Its Impact
units.passage:
In October 2002, a series of bomb attacks occurred in Bali, Indonesia. The attacks took place in areas popular with tourists, including restaurants and nightclubs. Many people were killed or injured, including Indonesian citizens and foreign visitors.

The ***tragedy*** affected families, businesses, and the tourism industry. Bali was known as a popular holiday destination, but the attacks created fear among visitors. Many hotels, restaurants, and travel businesses experienced difficulties after the incident.

The bombing also encouraged greater attention to security and cooperation between countries. Indonesia and other nations worked to prevent terrorism and protect public safety. The event remains an important part of Indonesia's modern history.

units.title: Reformasi 1998
units.passage:
In 1998, Indonesia experienced a major political change known as Reformasi. Before this period, President Suharto had led the country for many years. Economic problems and public dissatisfaction increased during the late 1990s. Many students and citizens demanded political reform.

Demonstrations took place in several cities. Students called for greater freedom, less corruption, and a more democratic government. In May 1998, Suharto ***resigned*** from the presidency. His resignation marked an important beginning of political change in Indonesia.

After Reformasi, Indonesia introduced several changes in its political system. People gained greater opportunities to express their opinions, and elections became more competitive. Reformasi continues to influence Indonesian politics today.

units.title: The Free Nutritious Meal Program
units.passage:
The Free Nutritious Meal Program, commonly known as Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG), is a government program designed to provide nutritious food to students and other selected groups. The program aims to support children's health and improve their ability to learn at school.

A nutritious meal usually contains carbohydrates, protein, vitamins, and minerals. These nutrients help the body grow and provide energy for daily activities. Students who receive ***adequate*** nutrition may find it easier to concentrate during lessons.

However, the program requires careful planning. Food must be prepared safely, delivered on time, and stored at the correct temperature. Schools and food providers need to follow hygiene standards to prevent food contamination. Regular monitoring is also important to ensure that the meals are healthy and safe.

units.title: Plastic Pollution
units.passage:
Plastic is widely used because it is light, inexpensive, and strong. People use plastic bags, bottles, food containers, and many other products every day. However, plastic waste has become a serious environmental problem.

Many plastic products are used only once and then thrown away. Some plastic waste enters rivers and oceans. Animals may eat plastic or become trapped in it. Plastic can also break into very small pieces called microplastics, which may remain in the environment for a long time.

People can reduce plastic pollution by using ***reusable*** bags and bottles. Recycling is also helpful, but reducing the use of unnecessary plastic is an important first step. Governments and communities can support these efforts through education and waste management programs.

units.title: Sleep and Student Health
units.passage:
Sleep is important for the physical and mental health of university students. During sleep, the body repairs itself and the brain processes information. Students who sleep well may have better concentration and memory.

Many students stay up late to study or use their phones. However, lack of sleep can make them tired and ***reduce*** their ability to focus. It may also affect their mood and academic performance.

Health experts generally recommend that adults get enough sleep every night. Students can improve their sleep habits by keeping a regular schedule, avoiding caffeine late in the day, and reducing screen time before bed. Good sleep habits can help students feel healthier and perform better.

units.title: Urban Farming in the City
units.passage:
Urban farming is the practice of growing plants and raising animals in urban areas. Many people grow vegetables, fruits, and herbs in their gardens, on rooftops, or in small spaces near their homes. Urban farming has become popular in many cities because it provides fresh food and helps people use available land more effectively. Even people who live in apartments can grow plants in containers or small pots.

One of the main benefits of urban farming is that it gives people access to fresh and healthy food. Vegetables grown at home can be ***harvested*** when they are ready to eat. This means that people do not need to buy all their vegetables from supermarkets. Urban farming can also reduce transportation costs because food does not have to travel long distances from farms to consumers.

Urban farming also brings social benefits. People who work together in community gardens can share knowledge, tools, and seeds. They can learn how to grow different plants and how to take care of the environment. In some neighborhoods, community gardens become places where people meet, talk, and build friendships. Children can also learn about plants, food, and nature through gardening activities.

However, urban farming has some challenges. Cities often have limited space, and not all buildings have suitable areas for growing plants. Plants also need enough sunlight, water, and good soil to grow properly. Some urban areas have polluted soil, so people must be careful when choosing places for gardening. Despite these challenges, urban farming continues to develop as a useful activity for city residents.
